en: The Ṣaṇmukhī Dhāraṇī. Oṃ, homage to the Buddha!

Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in the great circular assembly hall, situated in the expanse of the sky above the Pure Abodes, adorned with a manifold array of various jewels distinguished by the seven precious gems.
Together with an incalculable multitude of Bodhisattvas.
Thereupon, the Blessed One addressed the bodhisattvas.
O sons of noble family, you should all take up this dhāraṇī named Ṣaṇmukhī for the benefit of the entire world.
It is as follows:
[1] Whatever experience of suffering I may have while wandering in saṃsāra, may it not be characterized by a lack of realization through the equality of all things.
[2] And whatever experience of worldly prosperity and happiness I may have, may it be for the common enjoyment of all sentient beings. [3]

And whatever slight evil karma, root of unwholesomeness, or karmic obscuration I may have, may it not remain unconfessed, but be confessed through the unsurpassed confession. And whatever deeds of Māra I may have, may they not remain unrecognized, but be recognized through the unsurpassed recognition.
Whatever root of merit I have accumulated through the perfections, whether mundane or supramundane, may that become the unsurpassed wisdom of all sentient beings.
May my own liberation be for the sake of the liberation of all sentient beings. And may I not abide in either saṃsāra or nirvāṇa.
It is as follows:
Oṃ kṣame kṣame | kṣānte kṣānte | dame dame |
O tamed one, O tamed one! O auspicious one, O auspicious one! O most auspicious one, O most auspicious one!
Candre candre | Sucandre sucandre | Candra-kiraṇe |
Candravatī | Tejavatī | Dhanavatī |
Possessing the Dharma.
Possessing the Brahman;
the purifier of all afflictions;
the accomplisher of all aims.
It pacifies all misfortunes,
accomplishes the ultimate truth,
and purifies the body.
Or the purifier of speech;
the purifier of mind, svāhā!

Whosoever, whether a son of good family or a daughter of good family, shall recite this dhāraṇī named Ṣaṇmukhī three times by night and three times by day, having exhausted all karmic obscurations, will swiftly awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One; and those bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, with uplifted minds, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
The Noble Dhāraṇī Named "Six-Faced" is Complete.
